mainTopic: Arrow-שחיטה and כיסוי הדם, knife length and small blades, and whether שחיטה and טבילה require כוונה
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of רבי יונה בר תחליפא, who slaughtered a flying bird with an arrow. The torn feathers prove the cut came from the front of the neck. He set aside the earth of the whole valley ahead of time, so there was 'earth below' for כיסוי הדם. Next, רבי זירא explains the משנה's case of cutting off the head in one stroke: the knife must be the width of the neck plus another full neck-width. רב מנשה limits the משנה's permission to use a scalpel to one without pointed corners. The גמרא then discusses whether a needle or a cobbler's needle may be used. A new משנה rules that a knife which fell by itself and slaughtered makes the animal פסולה. The גמרא infers that a knife a person dropped is כשרה even without intent, and רבא says this follows רבי נתן, who allows a knife thrown at a wall. Finally, רב and רבי יוחנן disagree about a נדה who was forced to immerse, and רב נחמן tries to prove from a falling wave that חולין need no כוונה. The גמרא questions that proof, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The torn feathers show the cut came from the front
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we know the arrow cut the bird's neck from the front because the feathers there were torn apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can tell because the feathers at the front of the neck were torn open by the arrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier question about the arrow-שחיטה of רבי יונה בר תחליפא. The torn feathers prove the cut went through the front of the neck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A valid שחיטה must cut the סימנים from the front of the neck. When an arrow flies through a bird's neck, you might worry it entered from the back. The feathers at the front were torn open, which is clear physical evidence of the arrow's path.

keyTerms.meaning: Feathers (or wing-feathers) of a bird
That are torn apart or unraveled

phrases.english: Feathers that are torn apart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous section about how we know the arrow cut the neck in a valid way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Physical evidence: the state of the feathers shows where the arrow went.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the arrow came in from the back of the neck, which would make the שחיטה invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The torn feathers at the front show the cut was from the front, so the שחיטה is valid.

steps.title: But the blood needs to be covered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new problem: a bird's blood requires כיסוי הדם, so how could this arrow-שחיטה work?
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't the bird's blood need to be covered?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge to the arrow-שחיטה. Bird blood must be covered with earth, so the practice needs to fit that מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a wild animal or a bird is slaughtered, the תורה requires covering its blood. When the bird is shot in mid-air, the blood falls wherever the bird happens to be. The גמרא asks how the מצוה could be done properly in that situation.

keyTerms.meaning: Covering, meaning the מצוה of כיסוי הדם, covering the blood of a slaughtered bird or wild animal
Requires or needs

phrases.english: But it requires covering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the cutting question settled, the גמרא raises a second difficulty about the same arrow-שחיטה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of רבי יונה בר תחליפא of slaughtering a flying bird with an arrow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The blood of a bird must be covered, and it is unclear how that can be done properly when the bird is shot in the air.

steps.title: Covering afterward is not enough: earth is needed below and above
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the easy answer that he simply covered the blood afterward. Based on the פסוק, רב requires earth beneath the blood as well as on top of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he covered it afterward, that is not enough. רבי זירא said in the name of רב: one who slaughters must put earth below the blood and earth above it. The פסוק says 'and cover it in earth,' not just 'earth.' This teaches that the blood must have earth both below and above it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a simple answer: he just covered the blood. Then it knocks that answer down using רב's teaching that earth is also needed underneath the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בֶּעָפָר means 'in earth,' so the blood has to end up inside the earth, with a layer beneath it and a layer above it. Covering the blood afterward only gives earth on top. Blood that falls from the sky onto random ground seems to have no proper earth prepared underneath, so the challenge becomes stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: the גמרא suggests a possible answer, usually so it can reject it
Earth below and earth above the blood
'And cover it in earth,' the פסוק about כיסוי הדם
This teaches: introduces what we learn from the wording of the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is asking whether he covered the blood at all. The real problem is the earth that needs to be beneath the blood before it falls.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב's rule of earth below and earth above is the practical way כיסוי הדם is done: earth is put down before the שחיטה and more earth is added on top afterward.

phrases.english: And if you would say that he covers it,
but didn't Rabbi Zeira say that Rav said:
One who slaughters must place
earth below and earth above,
as it is stated: 'And cover it in earth,'
It does not say 'earth' but 'in earth,'
which teaches that one who slaughters must place
earth below and earth above!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דִּמְכַסּוּ לֵיהּ, וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge from step 2 by suggesting a simple answer and rejecting it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggested answer that covering the blood afterward solves the problem.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Covering afterward gives only earth above. רב's reading of בֶּעָפָר also requires earth beneath the blood.
steps.kashyaTarget: The arrow-שחיטה of a flying bird.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood falling from the air lands on ground that was not prepared as the 'earth below' that רב requires.

steps.title: He set aside the earth of the whole valley in advance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יונה בר תחליפא designated the earth of the entire valley beforehand, so wherever the blood fell, there was earth below it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He designated for himself the earth of the whole valley ahead of time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the כיסוי הדם challenge. Before shooting, he set aside the earth of the entire valley to serve as the 'earth below.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'earth below' does not have to be spread out by hand. Ground that was set aside ahead of time for this purpose also counts. Since the whole valley was designated, the blood lands on proper earth wherever it falls, and he then covers it with earth on top.

keyTerms.meaning: That he designates or prepares in advance
A valley or open stretch of land

steps.whatToRemember: The arrow-שחיטה works because the feathers prove the cut came from the front, and the valley's earth was set aside ahead of time as the 'earth below' for כיסוי הדם.

phrases.english: That he designates for himself the earth
of the entire valley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in steps 2 and 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the case: the earth below was prepared in advance by designating the whole area.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood landing from the air has no prepared earth beneath it, so כיסוי הדם cannot be done properly.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the whole valley's earth was designated ahead of time, there is earth below wherever the blood falls, and he covers it on top afterward.

steps.title: Cutting off the head in one motion: the knife must be longer than the neck
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's case of someone who cut off the head in one stroke. רבי זירא rules that the knife must be as wide as the whole neck and extend beyond it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if he was slaughtering and cut off the head in one stroke, it is valid if the knife is as long as the neck. רבי זירא said: it must be the full width of the neck plus more beyond the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה's case of cutting off the head in one motion. רבי זירא then explains exactly how long the knife must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows cutting off the head in one stroke if the knife is as long as the neck. רבי זירא adds that a knife exactly as wide as the neck is not enough. It must also stick out past the neck, so the knife is drawn across the neck and not just pushed through it.

keyTerms.meaning: Cut off (the head) in one stroke
The full width of the neck
Beyond the neck: extra length past the neck

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new discussion about the minimum length of a slaughtering knife when the head is cut off in a single stroke.

phrases.english: If he was slaughtering and cut off the head,
Rabbi Zeira said:
The full width of the neck and beyond the neck.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה שׁוֹחֵט וְהִתִּיז, אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the arrow discussion is finished, and the גמרא goes back to explain a line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the head is cut off in one stroke, the knife must be the full width of the neck and also extend beyond it.

steps.title: How much extra length does the knife need?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי זירא's 'beyond the neck' means an extra full neck-width or just any small extra amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: does 'the whole neck and beyond the neck' mean beyond it by a whole neck's width, so the knife is two necks long? Or does it mean the whole neck plus just a little bit more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is asking a question about רבי זירא's rule from step 5. How much 'extra' does the knife need?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said the knife must be as wide as the neck and stick out past it. That leaves the size of the extra unclear. The two options are a full extra neck-width (two necks in total) or just a tiny bit (מַשֶּׁהוּ).

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars, an open problem waiting for a solution
Any small amount

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:

phrases.aramaic: מְלֹא צַוָּאר וְחוּץ לַצַּוָּאר כִּמְלֹא צַוָּאר,
phrases.english: Does it mean the full neck, and beyond the neck by another full neck,
so that the knife comes to two necks long,
or perhaps
it means the full neck and beyond the neck by any small amount?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what exactly רבי זירא's rule in step 5 requires
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the 'beyond the neck' in רבי זירא's rule means an extra full neck-width or any small extra

steps.title: A source about cutting two heads at once
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a source: if someone cut two heads in one stroke, it is כשר if the knife has 'one full neck.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone was slaughtering and cut off two heads at once, and the knife has the length of one full neck, the שחיטה is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to try to answer the question. This step only quotes the source. The next steps will work out what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case has two animals cut together in one stroke. The source says 'one full neck' is enough. The גמרא will now ask what that phrase means and use it to settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Cut off completely, so the head comes off
At one time, in one stroke
Valid, so the שחיטה works

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If one was slaughtering and cut off
two heads in one stroke,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ לַסַּכִּין מְלֹא צַוָּאר אֶחָד – כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: if the knife has the length of one full neck, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question in step 6
steps.raayaObject: How much extra length the knife needs past the neck
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of cutting two heads at once with a knife of 'one full neck'

steps.title: It cannot mean only one neck
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects reading 'one full neck' as just one neck. One animal already needs more than that, so two animals surely need more.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'one full neck' mean? If you say it means just one neck and nothing more, that makes no sense. For one animal we need the whole neck and more. Could one neck's length be enough for two animals?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'one full neck' means. It rules out the simple reading of 'just one neck.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: From רבי זירא we know that even one animal needs a knife longer than its neck. So a knife only one neck long can't be enough for two necks at once. The phrase must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you would say, which brings up a reading in order to reject it
And nothing more
Now, used to set up a 'how much more so' argument
Is enough

phrases.english: What is meant by 'one full neck'?

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא מְלֹא צַוָּאר אֶחָד וְתוּ לָא,
phrases.english: If you say it means one full neck and nothing more,
now, if for one animal
we need the full neck and beyond the neck,
then for two animals
is the length of one full neck enough for them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מְלֹא צַוָּאר אֶחָד? אִילֵּימָא מְלֹא צַוָּאר אֶחָד וְתוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts working out the meaning of the source from step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that 'one full neck' means only one neck's length
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would let two animals get by with less than one animal needs under רבי זירא's rule

steps.title: It means one extra neck beyond the two necks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'one full neck' means one extra neck-width beyond the two necks being cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that it means one full neck beyond the two necks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reading of the source. The knife must cover both necks and stick out one more full neck-width.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the 'one full neck' in the source is the extra part, added on top of the two necks being cut. That extra part is a whole neck-width, not just a small amount.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
Beyond the two necks

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it means
one full neck beyond the two necks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the right reading after step 8 rejected the simple one
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'One full neck' means one extra neck-width beyond the two necks

steps.title: Proven: the extra must be a full neck
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי זירא meant the knife must stick out past the neck by a full neck-width.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: a full neck beyond the neck. Yes, learn it from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question from step 6. The extra past the neck must be a full neck-width.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the two-animal case the extra was a full neck. So in the one-animal case the extra is also a full neck. That means the knife must be at least two necks long. The option of 'any small amount' is ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, meaning the point is proven

steps.whatToRemember: For cutting off the head in one stroke, the knife must be the neck's width plus another full neck's width, so two necks long in total.

phrases.english: Learn from it:
a full neck beyond the neck,
yes, learn it from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reading in step 9 to answer the question in step 6
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The knife must stick out past the neck by a full neck-width, so it is two necks long

steps.title: A scalpel is allowed only if it has no pointed corners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next line about moving the knife back and forth. רב מנשה limits the permission to use a scalpel to one without pointed corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When he moved the knife forward and did not bring it back, and so on. רב מנשה said: this is about a scalpel that has no pointed corners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה. If you move the knife back and forth, even a tiny knife like a scalpel works. רב מנשה adds that this applies only to a scalpel without pointed corners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The long-knife rule only applies when you cut in one stroke. If you saw back and forth, any size knife is fine, even a scalpel. רב מנשה limits this. A short scalpel with pointed corners is not allowed, because the corners could poke into or between the סימנים and make the שחיטה פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? It limits the rule just stated
He moved the knife forward but did not bring it back
A scalpel, a small surgical knife
Literally 'horns': pointed corners sticking out from the sides of the blade

steps.confusionAlert: רב מנשה is not limiting the long-knife rule. He is talking about the משנה's next case: back-and-forth cutting, where even a scalpel is allowed.

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
When he moved the knife forward and did not bring it back, and so on.
רב מנשה said:
This is with a scalpel that has no pointed corners.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים – בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוֹלִיךְ וְלֹא הֵבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה after the knife-length question is settled
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's permission to use a scalpel for back-and-forth cutting applies only to a scalpel without pointed corners

steps.title: Can you slaughter with a needle?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא asks רב מנשה whether a needle may be used for שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב אויא said to רב מנשה: What is the law about a needle?
steps.whatsHappening: Right after רב מנשה's ruling about the scalpel, a student asks him a follow-up question: what about using a needle?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מנשה just said a scalpel works only if it has no pointed corners. The natural next question is about an even thinner tool, a needle.

keyTerms.meaning: A needle

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Avya, said
to Rav Menashe:
What about a needle?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question to רב מנשה's scalpel ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a needle is a valid tool for שחיטה

steps.title: A needle pierces instead of cutting
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשה answers that a needle pokes through the neck rather than cutting it, so it cannot be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A needle pierces.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשה answers that a needle does not work, because it pokes a hole instead of cutting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שחיטה has to be done by cutting across the סימנים. A round needle only punctures them, so it does not do a cutting action at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It pierces or tears through, rather than cutting

phrases.english: He said to him:
A needle pierces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about a needle
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A needle is not valid because it pierces rather than cuts

steps.title: What about a cobbler's needle?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא asks about a cobbler's needle, which is flat and has sharp edges.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law about a cobbler's needle?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא asks a sharper question: what about a cobbler's needle, which can actually cut?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular needle fails because it only pierces. A cobbler's needle has cutting edges, so the reason given in step 13 may not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: A cobbler's needle, flat with sharp edges

phrases.english: What about a cobbler's needle?
phrases.notes: This is a flat shoemaker's needle with sharp sides, so it can cut and not just poke.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the plain needle to a needle that can cut
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a cobbler's needle, which has cutting edges, is valid for שחיטה

steps.title: Proof from 'even any size'
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשה points to the משנה's words 'אפילו כל שהוא' and suggests they include a cobbler's needle.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We learned, 'Even any size.' Is this not talking about a cobbler's needle?
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשה answers by quoting our משנה, which says a knife of any size is fine, and suggests that this includes even a tiny cobbler's needle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that even the smallest blade is valid. Since a cobbler's needle is very small but can still cut, רב מנשה reads 'any size' as covering it.

keyTerms.meaning: Even the smallest amount or size
Is it not? (introducing a suggested reading)

phrases.english: He said to him: We learned:
'Even any size.'
Is it not referring to a cobbler's needle?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by bringing a proof from the משנה
steps.raayaObject: That a cobbler's needle is valid for שחיטה

steps.title: No, 'any size' means a scalpel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: 'any size' could mean a scalpel, not a cobbler's needle.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means a scalpel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by saying the משנה's 'any size' might only mean a scalpel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A scalpel is small, but it is bigger than a cobbler's needle. If 'any size' only goes down to a scalpel, the משנה tells us nothing about a cobbler's needle.

keyTerms.meaning: A scalpel, a small surgical knife

phrases.english: No, a scalpel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב מנשה's reading of the משנה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not the possible ruling about a cobbler's needle
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Any size' can be read as a scalpel, so it does not have to include a cobbler's needle

steps.title: But the scalpel is already mentioned separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the משנה mentions a scalpel on its own, so 'any size' must mean something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: The scalpel is taught explicitly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection: the משנה already names the scalpel separately, so why would 'any size' also mean a scalpel?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the scalpel already has its own mention, reading 'any size' as a scalpel makes the משנה say the same thing twice. That would suggest 'any size' means something smaller, like a cobbler's needle.

keyTerms.meaning: Explicitly, openly
It (the משנה) teaches

phrases.english: The scalpel is taught explicitly!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rejection in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'any size' means a scalpel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה names the scalpel separately, so 'any size' would just repeat it

steps.title: The scalpel line explains 'any size'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the scalpel mention is not a new case; it explains what 'any size' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is explaining: What is 'any size'? A scalpel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is not repeating itself. Mentioning the scalpel is how the משנה explains the words 'any size.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scalpel is not a second case. It is the explanation of the first one: 'any size' means as small as a scalpel. So the reading from step 16 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is explaining (the earlier words)

phrases.english: It is explaining:
What is 'any size'? A scalpel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the משנה's structure: the second phrase explains the first
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The scalpel is a separate case, so 'any size' must be smaller
steps.terutzMaskana: The scalpel defines 'any size,' so a cobbler's needle is not proven

steps.title: Logic supports the scalpel reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues it makes sense: if a cobbler's needle were allowed, the משנה would not need to tell us a scalpel is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. If you think it means a cobbler's needle, then once a cobbler's needle is allowed, do we need to be told about a scalpel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings logical support for the scalpel reading. If even a tiny cobbler's needle were allowed, it would be obvious that a bigger scalpel is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is: the bigger case goes without saying once the smaller case is allowed. Since the משנה does mention the scalpel, 'any size' must mean the scalpel itself and not something smaller.

keyTerms.meaning: This also stands to reason
If it enters your mind (if you were to think)
Is it needed? (It is obvious)

phrases.english: This too stands to reason,
for if you think it means a cobbler's needle,
now that a cobbler's needle is permitted,
does a scalpel need to be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support to the answer of step 18
steps.raayaObject: That 'any size' means a scalpel and not a cobbler's needle
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: once the smaller tool is allowed, mentioning the bigger tool would be pointless

steps.title: The scalpel still needed to be mentioned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the support: the scalpel had to be mentioned, so we would not ban a cornerless scalpel because of one with corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: The scalpel was needed. You might have thought we should ban a scalpel without corners because of a scalpel with corners. So the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the support. Even if a cobbler's needle were allowed, the משנה would still need to mention the scalpel for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A scalpel with pointed corners is not allowed (step 11). We might have thought the חכמים would ban every scalpel so people would not mix them up. The משנה mentions the scalpel to teach that there is no such ban, so the logic of step 19 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (to teach)
Let us make a rabbinic ban (גזירה)
Because of, out of concern for
Pointed corners (literally 'horns')
It teaches us (the new point)

steps.whatToRemember: The proof that a cobbler's needle is allowed was rejected, and so was the support for rejecting it. The גמרא ends this discussion without a clear proof either way.

phrases.english: The scalpel was necessary,
since you might have thought:
Let us ban a scalpel without corners
because of a scalpel with corners,
phrases.notes: This goes back to רב מנשה's ruling in step 11 that a scalpel with pointed corners is not allowed.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the logical support brought in step 19
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the supporting logic of step 19
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The scalpel mention has its own purpose: to teach that there is no ban on a cornerless scalpel

steps.title: A knife that fell and slaughtered by itself
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: if a knife fell and cut the animal properly, the שחיטה is still פסולה, because a person must do the slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a knife fell and slaughtered an animal, even though it slaughtered in the normal way, it is invalid. As it says, 'And you shall slaughter... and you shall eat': what you slaughter, you may eat.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that if a knife falls on its own and cuts the animal's neck, the animal may not be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the cut itself was perfect, no person did the slaughtering. The פסוק links eating to 'you slaughter,' so the שחיטה must be done by a person.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (start of a new משנה)
In its normal, proper way
Invalid (the שחיטה does not work)
'And you shall slaughter... and you shall eat'

steps.confusionAlert: The problem here is not a bad cut. The cut was perfect. The animal is פסולה only because no person did the slaughtering.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets up a basic rule: שחיטה needs a person's action. The גמרא will build on this.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If a knife fell and slaughtered,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשָּׁחֲטָה כְּדַרְכָּהּ – פְּסוּלָה,
phrases.english: even though it slaughtered in the normal way, it is invalid,
as it says: 'And you shall slaughter... and you shall eat,'
what you slaughter, you may eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A knife that falls and slaughters by itself makes the שחיטה פסולה, because the פסוק requires that a person slaughter

steps.title: Reading the משנה: a dropped knife is valid even without intent
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's wording 'fell', the גמרא infers that if a person dropped the knife, the שחיטה is כשרה even though he did not intend to slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason it is invalid is that the knife fell by itself. But if he dropped it, it is valid, even though he did not intend to slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה by drawing a hidden rule out of its exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a knife that 'fell' is פסול, because no person acted. So if a person caused the fall by dropping the knife, there is a human act and it is כשר. This is true even though he had no plan to slaughter. That suggests the משנה holds that intent is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason
But by inference (introduces a rule read out of the wording)
He dropped it (a human action)
He intends

phrases.english: GEMARA
The reason [it is invalid] is that it fell [by itself],
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה from step 21, about the knife that fell and cut the animal properly.

phrases.english: but if he dropped it, it is valid,
even though he did not intend [to slaughter].

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּנָפְלָה, הָא הִפִּילָהּ הוּא – כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the new משנה quoted in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A knife dropped by a person makes a valid שחיטה even without intent to slaughter.

steps.title: Which תנא says intent is not needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that שחיטה does not require כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that we do not need intent for slaughtering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to know whose opinion the משנה follows. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 showed that the משנה does not require intent. That is not obvious, so the גמרא looks for the תנא who holds this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא? (asks whose opinion a teaching follows)
Intent
We require

phrases.english: Who is the תנא
[who holds] that we do not require intent for slaughter?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא דְּלָא בָּעֵינַן כַּוָּונָה לִשְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule inferred in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that שחיטה does not require intent.

steps.title: רבא: it is רבי נתן, as shown by the knife thrown at a wall
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה follows רבי נתן. He quotes אושעיא's ברייתא: a knife thrown at a wall that slaughtered properly on the way is כשר according to רבי נתן and פסול according to the חכמים. אושעיא ruled the הלכה follows רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it is רבי נתן. אושעיא, the youngest of the group of Sages, taught: if someone threw a knife to stick it in the wall, and on the way it slaughtered an animal properly, רבי נתן says it is valid and the חכמים say it is invalid. אושעיא taught this, and he also said: the הלכה follows רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question: the משנה follows רבי נתן, who allows a שחיטה done with no intent at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא the thrower wanted to hit the wall, not the animal, and רבי נתן still calls it כשר. So for רבי נתן intent is not needed, which matches the משנה's dropped-knife case. אושעיא also ruled that the הלכה is like רבי נתן.

keyTerms.meaning: The youngest of the group of Sages
To stick it into the wall
In its proper way (a properly done cut)
Rules valid / rule invalid
The final ruling follows ...

steps.whyThisMatters: The ruling 'הלכה כרבי נתן' means that, in practice, a שחיטה can be valid even if the person did not intend to slaughter.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is Rabbi Natan,
as Oshaya, the youngest of the company [of Sages], taught:
If one threw a knife to stick it into the wall,
and it went and slaughtered [an animal] in its proper way,
Rabbi Natan deems it valid, and the Rabbis deem it invalid.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ, וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ:
phrases.english: He [Oshaya] teaches it, and he says about it:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Natan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי נתן, who allows a שחיטה done without intent, and the הלכה follows him.

steps.title: Didn't רבא already say this once?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רבא already said 'it is רבי נתן' on the משנה about a חרש, שוטה וקטן who slaughtered while others watched, so why say it again here?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבא already said this one time! We learned: all of them who slaughtered while others watched them, their slaughter is valid. We asked: who is the תנא who does not require intent for slaughter? And רבא said: it is רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא for repeating himself. He already linked an earlier משנה to רבי נתן for the same reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the start of the מסכת, the משנה said a חרש, שוטה וקטן may slaughter if supervised, even though they lack proper intent. There too רבא named רבי נתן. If one statement already teaches that the 'no intent' view is רבי נתן's, the second seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: One time (already)
And others watch them (supervision)
We said (the גמרא refers to its own earlier discussion)

phrases.english: But didn't Rava already say it one time?
As we learned: And all of them who slaughtered
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the חרש, שוטה וקטן from the first משנה of the מסכת (2a).

phrases.english: while others watch them, their slaughter is valid.
And we said: Who is the תנא
who does not require intent for slaughter?
And Rava said: It is Rabbi Natan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 24 as a repetition of an earlier statement by רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement in step 24 that the משנה follows רבי נתן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא already attributed the 'no intent needed' view to רבי נתן on the משנה of חרש, שוטה וקטן, so saying it again seems redundant.

steps.title: Both statements are needed: a child still means to cut something
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers צריכא. From the חרש, שוטה וקטן case alone, we might think it is valid only because they intend some kind of cutting. In the thrown-knife case there is no intent to cut at all, so we needed to hear it here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If רבא had taught it only there, I would say it is valid there because the person at least intends to cut something. But here, where he does not intend to cut at all, I would say it is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by showing that each statement teaches something the other does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש, שוטה or קטן does mean to cut, even if not for a proper שחיטה. The man throwing at the wall has no intent to cut anything. רבא's second statement teaches that רבי נתן allows even this, and that the משנה of the dropped knife fits that view.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (both teachings are needed)
He taught us
For some cutting in general
I might say no (it would not be valid)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי נתן, and so for the הלכה, a שחיטה can be כשרה even with no intent to cut at all. That is more than the case of a supervised חרש, שוטה וקטן, who at least mean to cut something.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the child case and the thrown-knife case are the same. The child intends some cutting; the thrower intends no cutting at all. That gap is why רבא spoke twice.

phrases.english: It is necessary [to state both],
for if he had taught us only there,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא מִיכַּוֵּין לְשׁוּם חֲתִיכָה בְּעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: [I would say it is valid] because he intends some cutting in general,
but here, where he does not intend [to cut at all],
I would say no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: showing each statement is needed for a different level of intent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the חרש, שוטה וקטן case alone, one would think רבי נתן allows it only where there is at least some intent to cut.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא's second statement teaches that רבי נתן allows a שחיטה even with no intent to cut at all, as with a knife thrown at a wall.

steps.title: The other direction of the צריכא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the צריכא. If רבא had only taught the thrown-knife case, we might think it is valid only because a mentally competent person threw it. That would not prove anything about a חרש, שוטה וקטן, so both statements were needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had taught us only here, I would say it works because it comes from the action of a mentally competent person. But there, where it does not come from a competent person, I would say no. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from step 26 by explaining the other side: why the thrown-knife case alone would not have been enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case has something the other one is missing. The thrown knife was thrown by a בן דעת, a person with full understanding, though he had no intent to cut. The חרש, שוטה וקטן do intend to cut, but they are not בני דעת. Since neither case can teach the other, רבא had to say 'it is רבי נתן' about both.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with full understanding, a mentally competent adult
From the force or action of

steps.whatToRemember: A צריכא shows that each of two teachings adds something. The thrown knife teaches that no intent to cut is needed. The חרש case teaches that the person does not need to be a בן דעת.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the thrown-knife case. 'There' is the case of the חרש, שוטה וקטן.

phrases.english: I would say it is because it comes from the action of a competent person,
but there,
where it does not come from the action of a competent person,
I would say it is not valid,
so it is necessary to say both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the צריכא begun in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each case teaches something the other cannot
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the thrown-knife case alone, one might think the שחיטה is valid only because a בן דעת set the knife in motion.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both statements are needed. One shows intent to cut is not required, and the other shows a בן דעת is not required.

steps.title: A forced immersion: רב and רבי יוחנן disagree
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens. A נדה was forced to immerse against her will. רב says she is permitted to her husband but may not eat תרומה. רבי יוחנן says she is not permitted even to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: a נדה who was forced and immersed. רב יהודה said in the name of רב: she is pure for her husband but forbidden to eat תרומה. And רבי יוחנן said: she is not pure even for her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new מחלוקת between אמוראים about whether a טבילה done without the woman's intent counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב splits the case. For her husband, the forced טבילה works, but for eating holy תרומה it does not. רבי יוחנן holds that a forced טבילה does not work at all, not even for her husband. This connects to the theme of whether an action works without כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her menstrual state, forbidden to her husband until she immerses
Was forced, against her will
Immersed in a מקוה
Pure for her house, meaning permitted to her husband
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן, eaten only in purity

phrases.english: It was stated: a menstruating woman who was forced and immersed,
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
She is pure for her house,
phrases.notes: 'Her house' means her husband. She may be with him again.

phrases.english: but she is forbidden to eat teruma.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
She is not pure even for her house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new sugya that continues the theme of acting without כוונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a forced טבילה permits a נדה to her husband but not to eat תרומה. רבי יוחנן: it does not even permit her to her husband.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב with a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן: according to רב, the forced טבילה lifted the severe כרת prohibition of being with her husband. So surely it should lift the lighter מיתה prohibition of eating תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: according to רב, who says she is pure for her husband but forbidden to eat תרומה, you permitted a sin of כרת. Do we even need to ask about a prohibition of מיתה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב's split ruling and says it seems backwards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being with a נדה carries כרת, which is a very severe punishment. Eating תרומה while impure carries מיתה בידי שמים, which is lighter. If the forced טבילה is strong enough to remove the heavier prohibition, it should surely remove the lighter one too.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin punished by כרת, spiritual cutting off, which is more severe
A prohibition punished by death at the hands of Heaven, which is lighter than כרת
Is it even a question? Used to say something should obviously follow

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the stricter-sounding word is the heavier one. Here כרת is the more severe punishment and מיתה בידי שמים is the lighter one. That is why רבא is so surprised.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman,
according to Rav, who says:
she is pure for her house but forbidden to eat teruma,
a sin of karet you have permitted,
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'was permitted' (round brackets). The corrected wording, in square brackets, says 'you permitted'.

phrases.english: is a prohibition of death even a question?

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲוֹן כָּרֵת הִתַּרְתָּ, אִיסּוּר מִיתָה מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a forced טבילה permits her to her husband but not to eat תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if the טבילה removes the heavier כרת prohibition, it should surely remove the lighter מיתה prohibition.

steps.title: Her husband counts as חולין, which needs no כוונה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that her husband has the status of חולין, and purity for חולין does not need כוונה. So the question is not how severe the punishment is, but whether the matter is holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: her husband is חולין, and חולין does not need כוונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends רב by changing the way we measure the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא compared the two prohibitions by how severe their punishments are. רב נחמן says the real question is holiness. Being with her husband is a חולין matter, so the טבילה works even without intent. תרומה is holy, so by contrast her טבילה for it does need כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-holy things
Intent, meaning to do the act on purpose
Does not need

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer moves the sugya from 'how severe is the sin' to 'how holy is the matter.' That is the basis for why רב treats her husband and תרומה differently.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Her husband is non-sacred,
phrases.notes: Her purity for her husband is treated like purity for ordinary, non-holy things.

phrases.english: and non-sacred things do not need intent.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעְלָהּ חוּלִּין הוּא, וְחוּלִּין לָא בָּעֵי כַּוָּונָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's קל וחומר from step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the measure: holiness, not severity of punishment, decides whether כוונה is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A טבילה that removes a כרת prohibition should surely remove a lighter מיתה prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her husband counts as חולין, which needs no כוונה. תרומה is holy and does need כוונה, so the קל וחומר fails.

steps.title: Proof from a wave that falls on a person and vessels
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן proves that חולין need no כוונה from a משנה. A wave of 40 סאה that falls on a person and on vessels makes them pure. Since vessels have no intent, the person, who is listed next to them, also needs no intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say this? As we learned: a wave that broke off with 40 סאה in it and fell on a person and on vessels makes them pure. Isn't the person like the vessels? Just as vessels have no intent, a person also does not need intent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a source from a משנה to support his claim that purity for חולין works without כוונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forty סאה is the amount of water a מקוה needs. The משנה lists the person and the vessels together and says both become pure. Vessels can never have intent, so if the person is treated 'like' them, a person must also become pure without intent. The 'מאי לאו' wording shows this is a reading of the משנה, not something the משנה says outright.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? A request for a source
A wave
Forty סאה, the minimum amount of water for a מקוה
Isn't it that...? Introduces a suggested reading of a source
Similar to, alike

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן tries to prove that purity for ordinary חולין matters works without כוונה, because a falling wave purifies a person just as it purifies vessels. The next step challenges this proof.

phrases.english: And from where do you say this?
As we learned in a mishna:
a wave that broke off and had forty se'a in it,
and fell on a person and on vessels,
they are pure.
Isn't it that the person is like the vessels?
Just as vessels have no intent,

phrases.aramaic: אַף אָדָם נָמֵי לָא בָּעֵי כַּוָּונָה.
phrases.english: so too a person does not need intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רב נחמן's claim in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that purity for חולין does not need כוונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a wave of 40 סאה falling on a person and on vessels, which makes both pure. The person is compared to the vessels, which have no intent.

steps.title: Maybe the person was waiting for the wave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the wave: perhaps the משנה is talking about someone who sat and waited for the wave to break, so he did have intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know that? Maybe we are dealing with a person who sits and waits, watching for when the wave will break off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's proof from the משנה of the wave. It suggests the person in that משנה may have been waiting for the wave on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן assumed the person in the משנה had no intent at all, just like the vessels. The גמרא says the משנה might be describing someone sitting by the water, waiting for the wave. Waiting like that is a kind of כוונה, so the משנה would not prove that חולין need no כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know? A phrase used to question a proof
Perhaps, maybe; offers another way to read the source
Sits and waits, watching on purpose for something to happen
The wave will break off from the sea

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying vessels need intent. It is only saying the person in the משנה may have had intent, so the proof about people falls apart.

phrases.english: From where do you know this?
Perhaps we are dealing with one who sits and waits,
for when the wave will break off,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the wave in step 31 by reading the משנה as a case where the person did have intent.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not רב נחמן's rule that חולין need no כוונה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the person had no intent, but the משנה may be about someone who sat and waited for the wave, which counts as intent.
